acv.quote: The account was worth about three hundred and twenty K a year.

header.reason: The international half of the account moved to Adyen's local acquiring and the US stayed. Adyen ran a test on the customer's own international traffic and showed results by country, while we answered with an average uplift and delivered our own market-by-market analysis three weeks late, after the test had finished. Elena says nothing could have been done, but the evidence points to a late and generic response to a new head of payments we had not met before the renewal.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Build an outreach play for when a customer hires a new payments leader, opening with a country-by-country approvals review before they pull the declines themselves.
findings.quote: the first thing he did was pull declines by country

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Arm the head of payments with a CFO-ready page that shows his own approval gap by market in dollars, instead of an average uplift.
findings.quote: I can't take an average to my CFO.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Pre-empt competitor traffic tests by offering our own per-country test on the customer's international traffic, and ask customers what Adyen's test results showed, since Stefan never shared them.
findings.quote: Adyen ran a test on a slice of their international traffic and came back with results by country.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Stop answering approval questions with the Authorization Boost average uplift claim, and lead with the customer's own approval rates by country, card type and issuer.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a fast-turnaround market-by-market approval report with decline reasons, and name the Stripe person who reviews it with the customer every month.
findings.quote: He asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month, and I didn't have a name.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Use 'approvals' and 'money left on the table' in place of 'authorization' and 'uplift' in our international payments messaging.
